reference.source: Standard endocrinology texts and thyroid hormone resistance literature
clinicalPearls: Characterised by reduced tissue responsiveness to thyroid hormone, most commonly from mutations in the beta thyroid hormone receptor (THRB)
The paradoxical biochemistry is a raised free thyroxine and free triiodothyronine with a thyroid-stimulating hormone that is not suppressed (normal or elevated)
Usually autosomal dominant, so a family history of similar abnormal thyroid function tests is common and very helpful
Clinical features are variable and mixed, because tissues differ in their receptor dependence; goitre is common, and tachycardia can occur where beta-receptor-independent tissues remain responsive
Often discovered incidentally when thyroid function tests do not fit the usual patterns of hyper- or hypothyroidism
Most patients are clinically euthyroid overall and require no thyroid-directed treatment, as elevated hormone levels compensate for the resistance
The key differential is a thyroid-stimulating-hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma, which produces a similar biochemical picture but is a distinct disorder
reference.pathophysiology: Resistance to thyroid hormone usually results from dominant-negative mutations in the beta isoform of the thyroid hormone receptor. The mutant receptor binds hormone poorly yet still occupies target genes, interfering with normal receptor function. Because the pituitary and hypothalamus rely on the beta receptor for feedback, they sense hormone inadequately and continue to drive thyroid-stimulating hormone despite high circulating thyroid hormone. Peripheral tissues vary in their reliance on the affected receptor, so the same person can show features of both hormone excess and deficiency depending on the tissue.
additionalDifferentials: Assay interference or heterophile antibodies producing spurious results
Non-thyroidal illness affecting thyroid function tests
additionalInvestigations: Repeat and confirmatory thyroid function tests including free thyroxine, free triiodothyronine, and thyroid-stimulating hormone
THRB genetic testing and family screening
Alpha-subunit measurement and dynamic testing to exclude a pituitary adenoma
Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging when an adenoma is suspected
Assay interference checks such as alternative platforms or dilution studies
Markers of peripheral thyroid hormone action such as sex hormone binding globulin
redFlags: Features suggesting a thyroid-stimulating-hormone-secreting adenoma such as a pituitary mass or visual field defect
Inappropriate antithyroid or ablative treatment causing iatrogenic hypothyroidism
Severe or homozygous disease presenting in childhood with growth and developmental problems
reference.prognosis: Most people with resistance to thyroid hormone lead normal lives without specific treatment because compensatory high hormone levels maintain a euthyroid state; the main harm comes from misdiagnosis leading to unnecessary antithyroid therapy or thyroid ablation.
pitfalls: Misreading the raised hormones with unsuppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone as ordinary hyperthyroidism and prescribing antithyroid drugs
Failing to distinguish the condition from a thyroid-stimulating-hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma
Ablating the thyroid and creating lifelong management difficulty
Not checking family members with similar unexplained results
references: Specialist reviews of resistance to thyroid hormone
